subject: ss-neurosurgery
title: Hydrocephalus and NPH: DESH, tap test, ETV and Dandy-Walker

steps.say: Blockage inside the ventricles is producing obstructive disease, commonest at the aqueduct. Failed absorption at the granulations is producing communicating disease after bleeds or meningitis. Four chambers are sharing one circulation.
steps.tx: **Obstructive hydrocephalus** blocks CSF flow inside the ventricles, commonest at the aqueduct, while communicating hydrocephalus blocks absorption at arachnoid granulations after bleed or meningitis; all 4 ventricles share one downstream circulation. The site of block sets the operation. Imaging names the level before any tube is placed.

steps.say: A frond-like ventricular tumour in a child is overproducing fluid and it is cured by total removal. Removing the source is stopping the flood at its origin. Invasion on imaging is warning of carcinoma instead. Margins are confirmed on postoperative scans.
steps.tx: **Choroid plexus papilloma** causes CSF overproduction in children with a vividly enhancing frond-like ventricular tumour, cured by total resection that removes the source. Postoperative scans confirm complete removal. Overproduction overwhelms normal absorption. Invasion of parenchyma instead marks carcinoma with a different plan.

vis.alt: Coronal brain with intraventricular tumour, parenchymal invasion, obstructive hydrocephalus, MRI and histology panels.
vis.caption: Intraventricular choroid plexus tumour with hydrocephalus; papilloma overproduces CSF while carcinoma invades. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Three features are defining NPH in the elderly: wet, wobbly and wacky. Gait apraxia is leading, incontinence is following and dementia is trailing. Ventricles are outgrowing the sulcal atrophy on MRI.
steps.tx: Normal pressure hydrocephalus presents with 3 features, the **wet wobbly wacky** triad of incontinence, gait apraxia and dementia, with ventriculomegaly out of proportion to atrophy on MRI. Gait responds best to shunting. Dementia responds least once established. Early shunting is preserving more function.

steps.say: Tight high-convexity sulci with wide Sylvian fissures are marking shunt-responsive imaging. The callosal angle is dropping below ninety degrees. These signs are separating NPH from plain atrophy.
steps.tx: Disproportionately enlarged subarachnoid spaces (**DESH**) with high-convexity tightness of sulci and an acute callosal angle below 90 degrees mark shunt-responsive NPH imaging. Atrophy widens sulci everywhere instead. The angle is measured on coronal MRI through the posterior commissure. Radiologists are reporting it routinely now.

vis.alt: Axial MRI comparing normal brain with NPH brain showing enlarged ventricles, widened Sylvian fissures and compressed high-convexity sulci.
vis.caption: NPH brain with enlarged ventricles, widened Sylvian fissures and compressed sulci beside normal. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Forty millilitres are drained at the tap test with gait timed before and after. Objective improvement is predicting shunt response strongly. No improvement is leading to extended drainage before shunt is excluded.
steps.tx: The **tap test** uses a 40 mL drain or more (usually 40 to 50 mL) of CSF with timed gait and cognitive testing before and after, and objective gait improvement predicts shunt response. A single negative tap does not exclude NPH. External lumbar drainage extends the trial when doubt remains.

steps.say: Tectal tumours and webs are blocking the aqueduct in the young. A third-ventricle opening is bypassing the block without hardware. Shunts are avoided when the rest of absorption is healthy.
steps.tx: Aqueduct stenosis from tectal glioma or webs is treated by endoscopic **third ventriculostomy** rather than shunting, bypassing the block at the floor of the 3rd ventricle. One internal opening replaces lifelong hardware. Webs and benign tectal lesions suit it best.

vis.alt: VP shunt anatomy with ventricular catheter and valve beside sagittal brain showing endoscopic third ventriculostomy fenestration.
vis.caption: VP shunt hardware beside endoscopic third ventriculostomy fenestration bypassing aqueduct block. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Dandy-Walker is combining a posterior fossa cyst with small vermis and high torcula. Cyst, ventricles or both are shunted by compartment. Aqueduct patency is deciding the configuration.
steps.tx: **Dandy-Walker** malformation combines a posterior fossa cyst of the 4th ventricle with vermian hypoplasia and elevated torcula, managed by shunting the cyst, the ventricles or both based on compartments. Each compartment needs its own drainage when disconnected. Imaging maps the connections first.

steps.say: Premature bleeds are temporised with reservoirs while protein and infection are settling. Permanent shunts are placed only once fluid is clear. Early shunting is inviting blockage and infection.
steps.tx: Post-haemorrhagic hydrocephalus of **prematurity** is temporised with ventricular reservoirs or drains, with permanent shunting only after CSF protein and infection settle. Reservoirs allow tapping without repeated punctures. Clear low-protein fluid earns the permanent shunt. Only trained clinicians tap reservoirs; families learn warning signs before discharge.
